prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1161; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a side impact at an intersection involving the insured vehicle and a third-party vehicle. The claimant reports a wrist fracture from the impact and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is listed as a named driver on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Requested the police report and statements from the scene.

Entry 3: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The other driver's account matches the claimant's description of how the crash happened.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photographs and the vehicle damage estimate. The damage is mostly consistent with the described side impact, though a few old scratches on the lower panel may predate this crash and are being noted separately.

Entry 5: Spoke with a neighbor who believes the car had body damage several weeks before the stated loss date. The statement is unverified and will be checked against repair records and prior photos.

Entry 6: Claimant has given the same account of the collision in each conversation, including sequence of vehicles, signal status and point of impact. No inconsistencies noted to date.

Entry 7: Medical records show the wrist fracture is a plausible injury for a crash of this type. Claimant reports no prior injury to the same wrist or arm, and none appears in the records requested so far.

Entry 8: Treatment followed a typical course, with follow-up visits tapering as the claimant's range of motion and pain improved. Provider notes describe steady recovery.

Entry 9: File reviewed with the neighbor's statement and the older scratches still open for follow-up. Remaining items are repair records and the prior photo request before a coverage and valuation decision is made.
